q: What fraction of the gap between our ideal-noise Lambda_{3/5}~8.7 at p=1e-3 and Google's device Lambda_{3/5}~1.04 is due to leakage, correlated cross-talk, readout error, and loss of decoder priors respectively?
basis: Direct discrepancy observed between our uniform circuit-level depolarizing Stim sim (~x8 suppression) and the paper's device (~x1.04). The paper flags leakage + correlated errors as major contributors; a calibrated multi-channel Stim + Pauli+ simulation could apportion them.
next_steps: Build a Stim noise model with per-gate depolarizing + leakage_flip + correlated CZ error channels calibrated from the paper's Extended Data tables; ablate each channel to zero and measure the change in Lambda_{3/5}.

q: How does the empirical threshold shift under decoder choice (MWPM vs correlated-matching vs BP+OSD vs neural-network decoders) and under DEM decomposition (decompose_errors=True vs full hypergraph)?
basis: We saw Lambda~1 at p~=1e-2 with PyMatching's plain MWPM on decomposed DEMs. Correlated-matching and BP+OSD are known to push the effective threshold higher; the paper uses a correlated-matching decoder for its headline numbers.
next_steps: Rerun the same Stim circuits through (a) PyMatching correlated_matching mode, (b) Stim's built-in belief-propagation + OSD via LDPC, (c) tensor-network decoder; report the p at which Lambda_{3/5}=1 for each.

q: What is the shot budget required so that Lambda_{d/(d+2)} is resolved within 5% relative uncertainty for d in {3,5,7,9,11} at p=1e-3, and does the budget grow as ~Lambda^d as theory predicts?
basis: At p=1e-3 our d=7 point produced only 29 logical errors in 4e5 shots (14% relative SE), and d=9,11 would need vastly more. This is directly relevant for planning any hardware experiment aimed at demonstrating Lambda>>1.
next_steps: Do a variance-budget calculation from the observed p_L values; extrapolate to d=9,11 assuming Lambda constant; then confirm empirically with a targeted d=9 run at p=1e-3 (likely 1e7+ shots).

q: Can we independently reproduce Google's distance-25 repetition-code error floor near ~1e-7 per round in simulation, and can we detect a bursty (cosmic-ray-style) contribution using synthetic injection of correlated multi-qubit error bursts?
basis: The paper's rep-code floor at 1.6e-7 per round (event-excluded) is the most striking low-probability number in the paper but is far below what a CPU-only 80-second sim can resolve. GPU-accelerated Stim sampling + injected correlated errors would let us test whether the observed floor is consistent with a Poisson tail.
next_steps: Build a d=25 repetition-code Stim circuit; run 1e9-1e10 shots on GPU (Stim CUDA sampler); add an ERROR_BURST channel firing at ~1e-8/round and check the tail histogram matches the paper's high-energy-event story.

q: How sensitive is Lambda_{3/5} to the exact stabilizer measurement schedule (Hadamard-CZ ordering, CZ layer count, measurement/reset placement) used in the Stim rotated-memory-Z generator versus Google's Sycamore-specific schedule?
basis: We used Stim's built-in schedule; the paper documents a Google-specific CZ ordering + dynamical-decoupling insertion in Fig. 1b. A different schedule can change effective circuit depth and correlated-error footprint, which changes Lambda even at identical per-gate noise.
next_steps: Emit Stim circuits from both (a) the built-in generator and (b) a hand-coded schedule matching Fig. 1b (including DD pulses on idle qubits); run identical noise + decoder; report the Lambda difference.
